t: That cut is clean, but the swelling worries me.
We are running low on clean cloth again.
People keep working on bad ankles and making them worse.
Wash the cut and check it again tonight.
Boil the oldest cloth. It will serve until we weave more.
Tell them rest is treatment, not laziness.
I will look at the swelling after the next dressing.
Keep the clean strips separate from everything else this time.
Send them to me before supper if the pain worsens.
We have done what we can today. Let the body work now.
The deer tracks cross the creek and disappear on stone.
I heard movement near the ridge before dawn.
Something has been following the same game trail as us.
Wait beyond the stones. The tracks return on the soft ground.
Sound travels badly on that ridge. It may have been farther away.
Check for wolf prints beside the deer trail.
I will take the creek side while you circle above.
We should leave before dawn and move without talking.
Bring the longer spear tomorrow. The brush is too thick for a bow.
If the trail stays cold, we turn back before dark.
The lower face is good stone, but it breaks in narrow pieces.
I found a dark vein behind the loose rock.
The supports creaked when we struck the north wall.
Use the narrow pieces for foundations. They will pack tightly.
Mark the dark vein and bring a better lamp.
Stop working that wall until the supports are checked.
I will brace the weak side before anyone swings again.
We should sort the stone before hauling another load.
Meet me at the face after the lamps are filled.
Leave the loose section alone tonight. It will still be there tomorrow.
More people came to the shrine this morning than last week.
Half the prayers today were about food, and the stores are not empty.
People keep asking what the last miracle meant.
Fear brings people in faster than gratitude does.
They may be praying for neighbors who have less.
Tell them what happened first. Meaning can wait until afterward.
I will speak about the event without pretending certainty.
We should visit the people who stopped coming, not only count arrivals.
Let us talk after the evening prayers when the shrine is quiet.
I need time before I turn that story into a lesson.
The grain sacks look lower than they did yesterday.
We have plenty of roots and almost nothing else.
Someone took a second bowl before the children ate.
The cook used more grain this morning. That may explain it.
Roots will feed us if people stop complaining about them.
Serve the children first and count the bowls at the door.
I will ask what came in before we start blaming anyone.
We should dry whatever keeps and eat the rest quickly.
Let us count the stores properly after supper.
There is enough for today. Tomorrow needs its own answer.
The new house still leaks where the roof meets the wall.
Three households are waiting for the next load of timber.
The old thatch will not survive another hard storm.
Pack moss into the joint until the builder can return.
The families with children should get the first finished walls.
Strip the worst thatch and replace it before the rain starts.
I will bring a ladder and look at the leak tonight.
We need to finish one house before breaking ground on another.
Tell them we have not forgotten. Timber takes time.
We will know what the roof needs after the next rain.
The wind changed while I was crossing the square.
Those clouds are moving faster than I like.
The morning felt warm, but the shade still has a bite.
Bring loose things inside before the wind strengthens.
The clouds may pass north. They did yesterday.
Keep your coat nearby. The warmth will not last after sunset.
I will check the roofs before the first rain reaches us.
The fields need water, even if the rest of us prefer dry feet.
We will see what the sky decided by evening.
I am going inside before the weather proves either of us wrong.
